## Labelling buckets (label_priority)

- Fixed seed 20261025. 1 = the 150 largest groups; 2 = every other group with a `mobile_number` sender; 3 = a random 150 of the rest (smallest md5(seed|group_id)); 4 = the rest. Buckets are stored in `label_me_state.json` and `label_me.csv`: a rerun or a new phone file never moves a group that has a bucket; 0 groups were bucketed for the first time in this run. A new group later is bucketed by the first run's cut-offs (bigger than the smallest bucket-1 group: 1; a `mobile_number` sender: 2; md5 key up to bucket 3's largest: 3; else 4), so bucket 1 can grow past 150.
- Group registry (`label_me_state.json`, key hashes only): keys new in this run 0, of which joined an existing group 0; new groups 0; pairs of existing groups a new message is like both of, kept apart 17 (the freeze puts such groups on one side); groups seen before with no message in this run 84.
- **Bucket 2 trimmed** (2026-10-26T21:43Z, `--trim-bucket2 400`, seed 20261027): the 331 bucket-2 groups labelled at that time stay (src/label_real.py walks a bucket biggest first, so these are mostly its largest groups), 69 of the 288 unlabelled ones were drawn (smallest md5(seed|group_id)) and the other 219 moved to bucket 4. So bucket 2 is no longer every mobile-sender group, and bucket 4 now holds 219 mobile-sender groups that were never eligible for bucket 3 (bucket 3 is a random draw of the non-mobile groups only). A new mobile-sender group joins bucket 2 only when its key is up to 0.2384 (the trim's rate), else bucket 4.
- **Bucket 2 is scam-enriched by design** (messages from ordinary mobile numbers are much more often scams than messages from bank / DLT sender ids): do not read bucket 2's scam share as the base rate, and read results over buckets 1+3 for something closer to the inbox.
